title: Forbidding equal valleys (second valley ≥ n+2) excludes leftover L=84 at m≥3
statement: On a Juggler CycleMin of length 84 at the residual floor 261, charging one valley at n and the other m−1 valleys at n+2 excludes every m≥3, either under joint-minima or under the odd-run height law.
counterexamples: L=84, o=53, m=3, n=261, θ≈0.002086, Lean constant 1: split n / n+2 RHS≈0.003515; height plus n+2 RHS≈0.002180; both exceed θ
Joint-style split never kills m=3 at this floor: fifty climb interiors at T(261)=4216 already exceed the gap even if the extra valleys go to infinity
Height-split would need the other valleys ≥ 281; n+2=263 does not supply that
notes: Unique visit of n is true and already recorded as juggler_cycle_all_valleys_equal. The leftover-killer reading is the only novel half and is false. Not a floor raise and not a halt theorem.
tested_range: L=84, m=3,4,31 at floor 261; constants 1 and 6/5; height-split search to n2=50000
